A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sodium transport is increased in erythrocytes from essential hypertension patients, and this increase is not due to the increased sodium influx but is caused by the increased Na/Na counter-transport.

the Na/Na countertransport in erythrocytes is a sensitive indicator of the sodium transport system and may be a useful tool for studying the mechanism of sodium transport and the pathogenesis of essential hypertension.
the erythrocytic Na/Na countertransport system, in the presence or absence of ouabain, is increased in patients with essential hypertension.
